quotes.text: Learn how to modify total amounts when customers change their selections during checkout.
This article has multiple variants. Fetch one of the following URLs to view specific content for your use case:

old_evidence.text: Recalculate amounts on your server. Don’t trust client-provided prices or totals.
Only update Sessions that are active and not completed or expired.
After confirmation, you generally can’t increase the amount.
Updating the `line_items` or `price_data` recalculates the Session total and taxes.
You’re responsible for keeping the client and server in sync.

findings: The November 7 capture is only a 14-line index at the canonical route. It provides the Checkout Sessions embedded-components and Payment Intents elements variant links, not their variant bodies or an updated account of server APIs, lifecycle behavior, taxes, or confirmation (new raw lines 5-14).

The April 21 full capture distinguishes the Checkout Sessions API with runServerUpdate, server line_items/price_data and recalculated Session total/taxes (old raw lines 28-178) from the Payment Intents API with server-calculated amount, paymentIntents.update, client refresh and later confirmation (old raw lines 180-247). These are historical, dated details, not November-verified variant contents.

Current summary correctly preserves both historical paths (source lines 11-13, 22-64), but frontmatter/raw list and Raw Sources only cite the April capture (source lines 4-8, 89-91). Add the November index as a separately dated navigational raw reference without promoting April behavior to November authority.

Current 'Security Rules (Both Paths)' tells readers to check status !== 'complete' and expires_at for sessions/intents (source lines 15-20), but the paired old raw restricts completed/expired checks explicitly to Sessions (old raw lines 19-26, 142-149). PaymentIntent and Checkout Session identities and state tests should be separated; a Checkout Session status/expiry check must not be presented as a PaymentIntent rule.

Current timing table merges PaymentIntent requires_payment_method/requires_confirmation labels with Checkout Session complete/expired labels (source lines 66-73). Qualify per API and retain the old raw's 'generally' qualifier for post-confirmation increase (old raw lines 23-26).

The April Checkout Session sample supplies one line_items entry in an illustrative server update (old raw lines 158-172; source lines 35-49); the summary should not promise preservation of an existing cart from that snippet. The PI computeOrderAmount function is a TODO placeholder (old raw lines 204-229), so it is not a ready-made pricing implementation.
substantive_changes: No supported change in payment behavior is established by the new root capture: the substantive content removed from the diff is replaced by variant navigation, without either variant body (diff lines 3-11, 248-249; new raw lines 9-14).

A source correction is warranted independently of the raw delta: the existing summary conflates Checkout Session status/expiry with PaymentIntent state (source lines 15-20, 66-73 versus old raw lines 19-26, 142-149).

source_assessments.reason: The root capture changes navigation/provenance, and the prior mapped summary contains an API identity/state conflation that is material even without a substantive November behavior delta.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/advanced/dynamically-update-amounts, new raw lines 5-14 establish only the purpose of modifying checkout totals and two variant destinations: Checkout Sessions API with embedded components and Payment Intents API with Elements. They do not state implementation prerequisites or a current state rule. The April capture, old raw lines 17-26 and 28-247, supplies dated server recalculation/authorization, Checkout Session runServerUpdate with line_items/price_data and Session status/expiry checks, and PaymentIntent server amount update followed by client refresh and later confirmation. The mapped source-stripe-checkout-dynamic-amounts.md summarizes those paths but wrongly extends Session status/expiry checks to PaymentIntents in source lines 15-20 and 66-73; its historical claims need dated provenance.
answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/advanced/dynamically-update-amounts, new raw lines 9-14 replace full guide bodies with variant navigation; the pinned capture establishes no substantive payment rule change. Keep April 21 behavior dated: old raw lines 17-26, 28-178 and 180-247 support server pricing, optional Checkout SDK beta flags, runServerUpdate, Session total/tax recalculation and PaymentIntent amount update/client sync, with the post-confirmation increase described as generally unavailable. In source-stripe-checkout-dynamic-amounts.md, source lines 15-20 and 66-73 require a reciprocal warning that Checkout Session complete/expired checks are not a PaymentIntent status/expiry rule; source lines 35-64 should not imply cart preservation or finished pricing code. Neither a server update nor UI refresh proves confirmation or payment success. The November linked variant bodies remain unread and unverified.
